sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: HTTP and REST questions are asked in every Python backend interview because everything you build will be an API. A fresher who can explain GET vs POST, 200 vs 404, and stateless vs stateful immediately earns credibility.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
**HTTP method intent:**

| Method | Safe | Idempotent | Use |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | yes | yes | Read |
| POST | no | no | Create |
| PUT | no | yes | Replace |
| PATCH | no | no | Partial update |
| DELETE | no | yes | Delete |

Idempotent = same result whether called once or many times.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **Status code groups** — 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error, 5xx server error. Know: 200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 500 Internal Server Error.
- **REST constraints** — stateless (each request carries all context), resource URLs (nouns not verbs), uniform interface.
- **JSON** — `json.loads()` string→dict, `json.dumps()` dict→string. The `requests` library auto-parses with `.json()`.
- **Authentication basics** — Bearer token in `Authorization` header. Never send password on every request.
- **`requests` library** — `requests.get(url)`, `requests.post(url, json=data)`. Check `.status_code` and `.json()`.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **'What is the difference between PUT and PATCH?'** — PUT replaces the entire resource; PATCH updates only specified fields.
- **'What does idempotent mean?'** — calling the same request multiple times has the same effect as calling it once.
- **'What is the difference between 401 and 403?'** — 401 Unauthorized means not authenticated; 403 Forbidden means authenticated but not permitted.
- **'What is stateless in REST?'** — the server stores no session state; each request is self-contained.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"REST APIs use HTTP methods to express intent — GET to read, POST to create, PUT to replace, DELETE to remove. Status codes tell the client what happened — 2xx means success, 4xx means client error, 5xx means server error. The stateless constraint means every request carries its own authentication token, which is why we use Bearer tokens in the Authorization header."*
